title: Quiz 2 — Standard Units
subject: Statistics
sourceText:
AP Stats — Quiz 2: Standard Units
Name: ________

A distribution of exam scores is roughly Normal with mean μ = 72 and standard deviation σ = 8.

We write a score x in standard units as
    z = (x − μ) / σ

Worked example: a score of 88 has
    z = (88 − 72) / 8 = 2
so it sits two standard deviations above the mean.

1) Convert 64 to a z-score.
2) A z-score of −1.5 corresponds to what raw score?
3) The empirical rule says about 95% of values lie between z = −2 and z = 2.
   State that interval in original exam points.

Note: once a value is in standard units, P(Z ≤ z) is read from a standard Normal table — the original units never re-enter the probability step.

marks.label: standard units (z)
marks.why: The quiz writes z = (x − μ) / σ without naming the move — that's how every later item talks about distance from the mean.

steps.text: A z-score asks: how many standard deviations is x from the mean?
Compute z = (x − μ) / σ. Same units cancel; z is a pure count.
Positive z is above the mean. Negative z is below. z = 0 is the mean itself.
In the worked example, 88 is 16 points above 72, and 16/8 = 2.

check.prompt: Apply the move: μ = 72, σ = 8. What is the z-score for x = 64?

marks.label: the 95% / two-sigma interval
marks.why: Item 3 cites the empirical rule in z-units but never shows how to put the interval back into exam points.

steps.text: The empirical rule: about 95% of a Normal distribution sits between z = −2 and z = 2.
To return to original units, undo the z formula: x = μ + zσ.
So the 95% interval on this quiz is 56 to 88 exam points.

check.prompt: Apply the move: μ = 72, σ = 8. What exam-point interval is z ∈ [−2, 2]?

nextLine.setup: A later problem says: 'A score of 80 has z = (80 − 72) / 8. Write the next line — evaluate that z-score yourself.'

expect.hint: Subtract, then divide: (80 − 72) is 8, and 8/8 is 1.
